question: Among strict historical Azores S1 taxa, does a named island have independently recorded vascular plant occurrences in a 2020 field survey, including any formerly extirpated island report? Not a historical resettlement or demographic rescue estimate.

source.title: Mapping Vascular Plant Diversity on São Jorge Island under the PRIBES project

loss_source.source_model: Author original Table S1, well-supported island-level only

predeclared_read_rules: Require publisher source archive signature and sane size <=10MB, compute immutable original source SHA256
Parse meta.xml and require Event core with unique ID and Occurrence extension with matching coreid link
Read only Event eventDate, island, location and Occurrence scientificName, taxonRank/basisOfRecord/status when present
Require calendar date >=2017-01-01 and <=2026-10-20; reject nominal year-only 2010 eventDate as field observation
Match strict Azores historical cases only by unambiguous literal/unique binomial name; do not fuzzy-synonym merge
Unique taxon×named island with at least one valid post-2017 field-event occurrence is observational re-detection only
Published historical local extirpation plus 2020 observation on same island is discrepancy or documented rediscovery candidate, never proof of colonization or previous loss mistake
No inferred zeros for taxa absent from a particular 2020 PRIBES survey: site/habitat effort differ
report_only: original core and extension row count
valid observed species names matched to strict S1 Azores taxa (aggregate counts only)
taxa observed on São Jorge in 2020 and historically extinct on same island, if any
distinct paired events and research provenance
